sections.h2: Is a quick sale realistic for an Easton house?
sections.html:
Yes. An Easton owner has three paths: hire an agent, handle the sale personally, or take an offer from a cash buyer who purchases as-is. Pick based on repairs needed, who occupies the house and your deadline. Deferred repairs, a tenant lease or a clouded inheritance are the common reasons an owner here looks at cash.

Easton is the seat of Northampton County, at the eastern end of the Lehigh Valley where the Lehigh River meets the Delaware. Phillipsburg, New Jersey, sits across the river, so some buyers commute over the bridges. The population was 28,127 in 2020 and 30,402 in July 2025. Owners live in 44.5% of the city's homes, so a good share of the houses you compete with are rentals.

The typical owner's home is worth $196,300 for 2020 to 2024, against a typical household income of $69,348. Citywide medians blur big differences between a renovated Downtown block and an unrenovated College Hill one, so price your house against recent sales close to it.

Easton is divided into four districts: Downtown, College Hill, South Side and West Ward. Lots are small and houses sit close together. Older ones often need a look at the roof, gutters and plumbing after a hard winter.

sections.h2: City offices that touch an Easton sale
sections.html:
Start with Code Enforcement, then the Historic District Commission, then the rental licensing desk if anyone rents the house. Code Enforcement administers the city Property Maintenance Code and the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code. Ask it whether any permits on your address remain open.

  • Permits: building, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving or demolishing a structure, changing its use, or installing electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems all need one.
  • Historic review: facade and signage work may also need a certificate of appropriateness from the Historic District Commission.
  • Occupancy cap: a single housekeeping unit may hold no more than three unrelated people, and an Occupancy Limitations Certificate states the limit for each dwelling unit.
  • Rental paperwork: an owner who rents files each tenant's name and address with the Rental Licensing Officer, and a moving permit comes from the Finance Department.
  • Fire check: the fire inspector will do a free fire safety inspection if you doubt a building has the required smoke detectors.

For a rented house, put the lease, rental license papers and tenant form in one folder. The buyer's attorney will want those papers, and having them ready saves days.

You will see separate tax bills from the city, the county and the school district. Easton levies 24.95 mills on the value the Northampton County Assessment Office sets. Residents also pay a city earned income tax of 1.45% plus 0.5% to Easton Area School District, for 1.95% in all.

The county mailed 2026 bills in mid-January. The discount ended March 31, and the face amount was due June 1. Taxes still owed when business closes on January 31 of the following year go to the Tax Claim Bureau. Clear any balance from the sale proceeds.

State realty transfer tax runs 1% of value. Pennsylvania law makes the person conveying and the person receiving jointly responsible for it. The Recorder of Deeds, at (610) 829-6210, collects it with any local tax at recording, and the city's tax list includes a real estate transfer tax. Ask for the combined rate at your price before you sign a contract.

Think the assessed value is high? The Assessment Division, second floor of the courthouse at 669 Washington Street, can give you the present appeal deadline. School homestead exclusions come from Act 72 of 2004, so an owner-occupant should ask the school district how the exclusion is handled when the deed changes.

sections.h2: What an Easton seller must tell the buyer
sections.html:
A seller of one to four dwelling units in Pennsylvania must give the buyer a written property statement under 68 Pa.C.S. section 7303. It must be filled in, signed and dated, and it is due ahead of the sales agreement. The state form runs through 16 topics, among them the roof, the basement, hazardous substances and title defects.

A seller who willfully or negligently falls short owes the buyer's actual damages, and a suit has to begin within two years after final settlement (section 7311). Executors and other fiduciaries selling for an estate fall outside the chapter (section 7302). Selling for cash does not alter these duties, so fill the form out honestly.

sections.h2: How a cash sale runs from first call to closing
sections.html:
You contact the buyer with the address and the facts that affect value: condition, tenants, open permits or code notices, and who holds title. The buyer weighs those facts and offers a price for the house in its present state. If you accept, a title search begins, and any lien, unpaid tax or estate question surfaces at that stage.

Before closing, gather the deed, the latest city, county and school bills, any lease and rental license records, and payoff letters for loans. An heir or executor should also bring the estate attorney's paperwork. Closing day means signing the deed and settlement statement. Whatever you owe in taxes or on liens is paid first from the price, then the deed is filed downtown in the Recorder of Deeds office. You hand over the keys when the funds clear, and you choose the date within what title work allows.

sections.h2: When cash is the better route
sections.html:
Cash fits best when condition, occupancy or timing would stall a listing. Typical Easton situations:

  • A house left by a relative that no heir wants to keep.
  • A rental where the unit or the license paperwork needs attention.
  • Open permits or code notices that scare off buyers who depend on a mortgage.
  • Roof, plumbing or heating damage after a hard winter.
  • A job transfer, divorce or court date that fixes your move.

A cash sale skips loan underwriting, a lender's appraisal and the repair haggling that often follows an inspection. Your closing date is limited mainly by title work. Weigh any cash figure against the likely net from a listing once repairs, concessions and transfer tax are subtracted. To get a figure for an Easton address, call or text with the details, including tenants and any open code items.

faqs.q: What controls the speed of a cash closing in Easton?
faqs.a: Title work and the date you choose control it, since there is no loan to underwrite. Once title is clear, the deed is filed and your payoffs are taken out of the price.

faqs.q: Who owes the Pennsylvania transfer tax in Easton?
faqs.a: The 1% state tax is the joint responsibility of whoever gives the deed and whoever receives it. Your sales agreement decides how the cost is divided, and the Recorder of Deeds collects any local share with it.

faqs.q: Is a tenant a problem when selling in Easton?
faqs.a: No, but paperwork matters. Owners who rent keep tenant names and addresses on file with the Rental Licensing Officer, so give the buyer the lease and those records.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for an Easton property?
faqs.a: The Northampton County Recorder of Deeds files deeds and mortgages and takes the fees and transfer taxes at the same time. The office number is (610) 829-6210.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Easton house?
faqs.a: Yes. Realty transfer tax does not apply to a transfer by will or intestate succession, and an executor selling for the estate need not give the disclosure statement. Settle title questions with the estate's attorney before setting a closing date.
